title: REST FOR OTHERS BEFORE REST FOR YOURSELF

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: However, your wives, your children and your livestock (I know you have much livestock) may stay in the towns I have given you, until the Lord gives rest to your fellow Israelites as he has to you, and they too have taken over the land that the Lord your God is giving them across the Jordan. After that, each of you may go back to the possession I have given you. - Deut 3:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses clarifies the arrangement: the families and flocks of the eastern tribes could stay in their towns, but the fighting men would remain in the battle "until the Lord gives rest to your fellow Israelites as he has to you." Only after their brothers were settled could these men return home to their own rest. Their own rest would wait until everyone had rest. This is a striking picture of selfless solidarity among God's people.

The key word here is "rest." God's goal for His people was rest — a settled place, freedom from conflict, security in the land He had given. And notice the beautiful principle: those who had already found rest were not to enjoy it alone while others still waited. They were to help their brothers into rest first. Their commitment to shared rest reflected a heart of genuine love.

This theme of rest runs all through Scripture and points us to something greater. The rest of the Promised Land was only a shadow of the deeper rest God offers His people. The writer of Hebrews tells us that there remains a Sabbath-rest for the people of God (Heb 4:9), a rest we enter through faith in Christ. Jesus invites all who are weary and burdened to come to Him and find rest for their souls (Matt 11:28).

And just as the eastern tribes helped their brothers into rest, we are called to help others find the true rest that is in Christ. Having found rest for our own souls, we long for others to find it too. We do not keep the good news to ourselves while others remain weary and lost. Let us labour, in love, to help our brothers and sisters into the rest that God gives, until all who belong to Him are safely home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you found true soul-rest in Christ?
2. How can you help others find the rest that God offers?
3. Are you willing to labour for others' rest before settling only into your own comfort?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You for the rest You give to my weary soul. Help me not to keep this rest to myself, but to labour in love so that others may also find rest in You, until all Your people are safely home. Amen.
